governing_table.code: Arkansas Plumbing Code (Arkansas Department of Health; based on the 2018 International Plumbing Code with Arkansas amendments). The building code (Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2021 Edition, Volume II) has no table of its own: its Chapter 29 reads only 'Refer to the Arkansas Plumbing Code.'
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1, based on the actual use of the building or space. Types of occupancies not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the State Administrative Authority. The number of occupants shall be determined by the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code. The occupancy classification shall be determined by the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code.
governing_table.building_code_quote: Chapter 29 Plumbing Systems. Refer to the Arkansas Plumbing Code.
governing_table.adoption_quote: Plumbing | 2018 Arkansas Plumbing Code, 9th Edition | Arkansas Department of Health
governing_table.amendments: Arkansas changes seen in Chapter 4 (UpCodes copy): occupants and occupancy class come from the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code; the state administrative authority may approve a lower actual occupant number; separate rooms for each sex are not required at 25 occupants or fewer (any occupancy); footnote g exempts banks, savings and loans and credit unions from providing public restrooms; Section 403.3(a) defines public restrooms; 404.1 sends accessibility to the Fire Prevention Code and the ADA. The table header still reads 'URINALS: SEE SECTION 419.2', but the urinal substitution rule is Section 424.2.
governing_table.source_note: healthy.arkansas.gov (the Department of Health's own copy) refused automated requests with HTTP 403, so the code text was read on UpCodes, a secondary copy.

fixtures.cities_may_amend_note: Read for the building and fire code only: local jurisdictions may adopt more stringent provisions on the base of the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2021 Edition (Section 101.2.2, Cornell copy of the State Fire Marshal's rule). Whether a city may amend the Arkansas Plumbing Code's fixture table was not read on any page: ask the Arkansas Department of Health, Plumbing and Natural Gas Section.
fixtures.cities_may_amend_quote: Each district, county, municipality, or other political subdivision of this state shall only adopt and enforce the provisions of the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2021 Edition. The AFPC 2021 Edition shall be the only foundation document available for modification by local jurisdictions should they choose to adopt more stringent provisions.

office.row_label: 2 Business (see Sections 403.2, 403.4 and 403.4.1): Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses (footnote g)
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: Optional. Section 424.2: may replace up to 50% of the required water closets
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink (water closets | lavatories | bathtubs/showers | drinking fountain | other)

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: Optional. Section 424.2: may replace up to 67% of the required water closets
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 | — | 1 per 500 | 1 service sink

school.urinals: Optional. Section 424.2: may replace up to 67% of the required water closets
school.quote: Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistics show a different split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, for each sex. Footnote a says the same: one fixture for the number of persons shown or any fraction of it.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. | a. The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational occupancies and up to 50% elsewhere. Each urinal needs a privacy partition.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load (employees and customers) is 25 or fewer, or in mercantile occupancies of 100 or fewer. The 25 figure is an Arkansas change (the model 2018 code is not quoted here because it was not read).
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 403.2 Separate Facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 25 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: The number of occupants comes from the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code (2021 IBC Table 1004.5): business areas 150 gross sq ft per occupant; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; educational classroom area 20 net. With the state administrative authority's approval, the actual number of occupants the space is designed for may be used even if lower.
occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Business areas | 150 gross ... Educational | Classroom area | 20 net || Exception: Where approved by the state administrative authority, the actual number of occupants for whom each occupied space, floor, or building is designed, although less than those determined by calculations shall be permitted to be used in the determination of the design occupant load.

stall_required.text: Each toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door; each urinal needs partitions at least 30 inches apart, starting no more than 12 inches above the floor and reaching at least 60 inches.
stall_required.quote: 405.3.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. | 405.3.5 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall be not less than 30 inches (762 mm). The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

banks_exception.text: Banks, savings and loan associations and credit unions are not required to provide public restrooms.
banks_exception.quote: g. Buildings, offices, or facilities maintained by banks, savings and loan associations, or credit unions for the conduct of their business shall not be required to provide public restrooms and are exempted from the section.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 1 = 0.5, so none.
50 women, 50 men. 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 2 = 1.
100 women, 100 men. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals up to 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 women, 200 men. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals up to 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals up to 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25/50 = 0.5, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals up to 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: The urinal limit applies 'in each bathroom or toilet room'; the figures assume one men's room holds all the men's fixtures.

hdpe_fire.section: Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2021 Edition, Volume II (2021 IBC with Arkansas amendments), Section 803.9, with 803.1.1 and the Chapter 2 definition of interior wall and ceiling finish
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286. Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | [BF] Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish. The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; ...
hdpe_fire.note: Section text read on UpCodes (secondary copy), which shows no Arkansas change to these sections. Adoption of the 2021 edition statewide read on the state's own list of current codes.

access.state_standard: ICC A117.1-2017, referenced by Chapter 11 of the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2021 Edition, Volume II (Section 1102.1; Chapter 35 lists 'ICC A117.1—17'). The Arkansas Plumbing Code adds a note that restroom clearances follow the federal ADA. Arkansas has no separate state accessibility code that was found.
access.state_standard_quote: 1102.1 Design. Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with this code and ICC A117.1. | ICC A117.1—17 Accessible and Usable Buildings and Facilities | (Arkansas Plumbing Code 404.1) Accessible plumbing facilities and fixtures shall be provided in accordance with the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code. NOTE: Restroom requirements for individuals with disabilities are covered under the Federal American with Disabilities Act (ADA) and not this code. Reference to the ADA should be made for clearance and spacing requirements for new or remodeled public facilities.

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall of an accessible stall
differences.state: A117.1-2017 604.5.1: the side wall needs a horizontal bar and an 18-inch vertical bar, bottom 39 to 41 inches above the floor, centerline 39 to 41 inches from the rear wall. Applies to wheelchair stalls (604.9.6) and to both sides of ambulatory stalls (604.10.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.' No vertical bar.
differences.quote: Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2. ... A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.point: Toe clearance under the front and one side partition of a wheelchair stall
differences.state: A117.1-2017 604.9.5.1: 12 inches high, extending 8 inches beyond the partition. Not required at the front if the stall is deeper than 64 inches (wall-hung toilet) or 67 inches (floor-mounted), or at the side if wider than 68 inches.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.4: 'a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition'; not required in a compartment greater than 62 inches deep (wall-hung) or 65 inches (floor-mounted), or greater than 66 inches wide.
differences.quote: The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members. Exceptions: Toe clearance at the front partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 64 inches (1625 mm) in depth with a wall-hung water closet, or greater than 67 inches (1700 mm) in depth with a floor-mounted water closet. Toe clearance at the side partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 68 inches (1725 mm) in width.

access.same_as_federal: Read and found the same: wheelchair stall 60 inches wide by 56 deep (wall-hung) or 59 (floor-mounted); ambulatory stall 60 deep and 35 to 37 wide; self-closing doors with pulls on both sides.
access.not_compared: Children's stalls beyond toe clearance, restroom door signs (703) and the count of accessible and ambulatory stalls (IBC 1110.2 vs ADA 213) were not compared line by line.
access.process: No state registration, fee or separate accessibility plan review was found. The Fire Prevention Code requires plans for certain classes of building to go to the State Fire Marshal 'if not approved by the local authority having jurisdiction' (Section 107, classes not read in full).

single_user.rule: Single-user toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures and are identified for use by either sex.
single_user.quote: 403.1.2 Single-User Toilet and Bath Fixtures. The plumbing fixtures located within, single-user toilet and bathing rooms that are required by Section 404 shall contribute toward the total number of required fixtures for a building or tenant space. Single-user toilet facilities and bathroom, and family or assisted toilet rooms and bath rooms shall be identified for use by either sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: The Arkansas Plumbing Code (2018 base) requires separate facilities for each sex wherever fixtures are required, with three exceptions (dwelling and sleeping units, 25 occupants or fewer, mercantile of 100 or fewer), and signs that designate the sex. It has no provision allowing a shared multi-stall all-gender room to count as the required facilities. Where each sex needs only one toilet, two family or assisted-use rooms may serve instead.
all_gender_shared.quote: 403.2 Separate Facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. | 403.4 Signage. Required public facilities shall be provided with signs that designate the sex, as required by Section 403.2. | 403.2.1 ... Where a building or tenant space requires a separate toilet facility for each sex and each toilet facility is required to have only one water closet, two family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall be permitted to serve as the required separate facilities.

use_restrictions.rule: Three acts. (1) Act 955 of 2025 (Ark. Code 22-3-2201 to 22-3-2203): a governmental entity occupying a public building (state departments and every political subdivision) must designate each multi-occupancy restroom for the exclusive use of females or males; single-occupancy and family restrooms remain allowed; the same act covers shelters (9-6-113) and state and local correctional facilities. (2) Act 317 of 2023 (Ark. Code 6-21-120): public school districts and open-enrollment charter schools, preK-12, must designate each multiple occupancy restroom or changing area for one sex and offer a reasonable accommodation such as a single-occupancy restroom. (3) Act 619 of 2023 amends the criminal offense of sexual indecency with a child (5-14-110) for adults who enter a public changing facility of the opposite sex for a sexual purpose knowing a minor is present; it sets no building requirement. None of these applies to private commercial buildings.
use_restrictions.quote: 22-3-2202. (a) A governmental entity occupying a public building shall designate each multi-occupancy restroom, changing room, and sleeping quarter for the exclusive use of females or males. ... (e) This section shall not be construed to prohibit a governmental entity occupying a public building from: ... (2) Establishing a single-occupancy restroom, a changing room, or sleeping quarter, or a family restroom, changing room, or sleeping quarter | 22-3-2201 (6) "Public building" means a building or related facility occupied by a governmental entity; (3) "Governmental entity" means every department, division, office, board, commission, institution, and political subdivision of this state | 6-21-120(b) ... each public school district and open-enrollment public charter school that serves students in prekindergarten through grade twelve (preK-12) in this state shall: (1) Require each multiple occupancy restroom or changing area to be designated as follows: (A) For the exclusive use by the male sex; or (B) For the exclusive use by the female sex
use_restrictions.note: Act 955 was approved 4/21/25 and has no emergency clause in the text read; its effective date and any court challenge were not read.

public_wage.law: None. The Arkansas Prevailing Wage Law (Ark. Code 22-9-301 to 22-9-315) was repealed by Act 1068 of 2017, approved 04/06/2017 with an emergency clause. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded work.
public_wage.quote: AN ACT TO REPEAL THE ARKANSAS PREVAILING WAGE LAW; TO PROVIDE FLEXIBILITY TO CITIES AND COUNTIES FOR CAPITAL CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS; TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY ... SECTION 1. Arkansas Code §§ 22-9-301 — 22-9-315 are repealed.
public_wage.note: The repealed law had applied where labor and material exceeded $75,000. labor.arkansas.gov refused automated requests (HTTP 403), so the Department of Labor and Licensing's own page was not read.

shipped_goods.rule: A remote seller must collect Arkansas state and local sales and use tax once its sales for delivery into Arkansas exceed $100,000 or 200 transactions in the current or previous year. If the seller doesn't collect, the Arkansas customer owes compensating use tax directly to the Department of Finance and Administration.
shipped_goods.quote: All remote sellers and marketplace facilitators are required to collect and remit Sales and Use tax to the State of Arkansas if within the current or previous year the sale of tangible personal property, taxable services, a digital code, or specified digital products for delivery into Arkansas exceeded one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) or two hundred (200) taxable transactions. (DFA) | 26 CAR § 30-201: If tangible personal property is purchased for use or consumption in Arkansas from a seller in another state and delivery is made in Arkansas, then such sale is subject to Arkansas compensating use tax. The out-of-state seller may be required to collect Arkansas tax. If the out-of-state seller does not collect Arkansas tax, it becomes the responsibility of the Arkansas customer to remit compensating use tax directly to the Department of Finance and Administration.

freight.rule: Delivery charges are part of the taxable price unless billed directly to the purchaser by a carrier other than the seller.
freight.quote: 26 CAR § 30-901(a)(1) Delivery charges are part of the gross receipts or gross proceeds on which the tax must be collected and remitted unless the charges are billed directly to the purchaser by a carrier other than the seller.

install_labor.rule: Labor to install, alter, replace or repair nonmechanical, passive or manually operated building components that become part of real estate (the rule lists walls, doors, locks, plumbing fixtures and 'similar components') is not a taxable service, in new or existing buildings. A separately stated installation charge is not part of the sales price unless it is a specifically taxable service. The rule does not name toilet partitions; the initial installation of 'furniture' is on the taxable list, so the classification of partitions should be confirmed with DFA.
install_labor.quote: 26 CAR § 30-1003(b)(1)(A) The initial installation, alteration, addition, cleaning (with exceptions noted in subdivision (c)(2) of this section), refinishing, replacement, or repair of nonmechanical, passive, or manually operated components of buildings or other improvements or structures affixed to real estate, including, but not limited to, the following: walls, ceilings, doors, locks, windows, glass, heat and air ducts, roofs, wiring, breakers, breaker boxes, electrical switches and receptacles, light fixtures, pipes, plumbing fixtures, fire and security alarms, intercoms, sprinkler systems, parking lots, fences, gates, fireplaces, and similar components that become a part of real estate after installation, are not taxable services. | 26 CAR § 30-102(8)(D) A separately stated installation charge is not part of the sales price and not taxable unless it is a specifically taxable service. | 26 CAR § 30-519(d)(4) If both taxable and nontaxable services are provided, the nontaxable charges must be separately stated on the invoice. Otherwise, the entire charge will be taxable.

furnish_and_install.rule: A contractor is the consumer of the materials used in a contract on real estate: the contractor pays sales tax when buying them (or use tax if bought out of state, or tax on withdrawal from stock), and materials used in nontaxable services are not taxed to the customer.
furnish_and_install.quote: 26 CAR § 30-1003(a)(1)(B) All contractors are deemed to be consumers or users of all tangible personal property including materials, supplies, and equipment used or consumed by them in performing any contract, and the sales of all such property to contractors are taxable sales. | (d)(1)(B)(i) Any materials used in the performance of nontaxable services are not taxed to the customer. (ii) However, the business must self-assess, report, and pay sales tax as a withdrawal from inventory (stock) on the purchase price of the materials. | (d)(2)(B) Use tax is required to be reported and paid on the purchase of materials from out-of-state sellers.

sales_tax.agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DFA)
sales_tax.note: 26 CAR § 30-1303 still states the compensating use tax as 6% of the sales price; DFA's rate table shows State Sales and Use Tax 6.500% since 07/01/2013. Local city and county taxes are added (the city agent covers them).

page.stalls_intro: Arkansas's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to two thirds of the toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: A space that holds 25 people or fewer, staff and customers together, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. Banks and credit unions don't have to provide public restrooms. These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Arkansas's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Arkansas's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and the access standard in Arkansas's building rules set the sizes. No separate state registration or review step for access was found, so plans go through the local building department.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Arkansas extras:** the access standard in Arkansas's building rules asks for two things the federal rules don't. The accessible stall needs an 18 inch vertical grab bar on the side wall as well as the horizontal one. The gap under the front and one side partition must be 12 inches high, against 9 inches federally, unless the stall is larger than the minimum.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom is marked for use by either sex. Arkansas's plumbing rules call for separate men's and women's rooms once a space holds more than 25 people, and they don't provide for a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask the Arkansas Department of Health before planning one. Arkansas law requires shared restrooms in buildings occupied by state or local government, and in public schools, to be designated for one sex.
page.public_jobs: Arkansas repealed its wage law for public jobs in 2017, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Arkansas, labor to install or replace parts of a building that have no moving machinery and become part of the property, such as walls and doors, is not taxed. The state's rule doesn't name toilet partitions, so confirm how yours are treated. A contractor who supplies and installs pays the tax on the materials instead of charging it to you.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, and so is freight the seller charges. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration
